name: Obsidian Sync
tagline: Paid sync service for a local-first Markdown knowledge base

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Sync listed at $5/user/month monthly and $4/user/month annually.
pricing.freeTier: Sync itself has no free tier, though the Obsidian app is free.

tiers.name: Obsidian app
tiers.limits: Free local Markdown app; 0 GB of hosted Sync storage included.

tiers.name: Sync Standard
tiers.limits: 1 synced vault, 1 GB storage, 5 MB maximum file size, 1-month version history and unlimited devices.

tiers.name: Sync Plus
tiers.limits: 10 synced vaults, 10 GB storage, 200 MB maximum file size, 12-month version history and unlimited devices.
tiers.notes: Storage can be upgraded to 100 GB; current add-on price was not publicly listed.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free Sync tier; the Obsidian app itself is free and stores local Markdown files
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every collaborator on a shared vault needs their own Sync subscription. Optional storage above 10 GB costs extra, but the current public amount was not found.

verdictSummary: If you already accept local Markdown files, syncing folders across devices is a solved problem; the hard part is not the app, it is conflict-free convenience.
coreLoopDIY: Use a local Markdown folder, git/Syncthing/iCloud/Drive for sync, and optional scripts for backlinks/search.
requirements: Syncthing, Git, iCloud, Dropbox, or similar
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for no-drama sync across devices while keeping Obsidian's local-first model.

priorArt.name: Syncthing
priorArt.desc: Open-source continuous file synchronization that can replace much of Obsidian Sync for tec

alternatives.name: iCloud Drive
alternatives.desc: Five free gigabytes and excellent Apple plumbing; everyone else gets a side door.

facts.install: Enable iCloud Drive in Apple-device settings; install iCloud for Windows from the Microsoft Store
facts.dataFormat: Ordinary vault Markdown files and attachments in Apple's iCloud storage, mirrored or downloaded into Finder, Files, or File Explorer on signed-in devices
facts.gapVsPaid: It is Apple-centric and lacks Obsidian Sync's vault-aware version history, deleted-file recovery, selective vault syncing and end-to-end-encrypted service across all supported platforms.
facts.setupBlocker: An Apple Account is required, free storage is shared with all iCloud data, and Android/Linux have no native iCloud Drive sync client

alternatives.name: Nextcloud
alternatives.desc: Your own cloud, complete with the privilege of maintaining your own cloud.

facts.install: Nextcloud All-in-One Docker stack or a supported web-server/PHP/database installation, plus sync clients
facts.dataFormat: User files in a server data directory or object store; accounts, shares, file cache, versions, and other metadata in the database, with optional local synced copies
facts.gapVsPaid: It can sync the folder, but it is not Obsidian-aware, does not provide the same conflict handling and version recovery by default, and makes you operate the cloud service.
facts.setupBlocker: A practical deployment needs an always-on host, Docker or a full PHP/database stack, domain and TLS, storage planning, backups, and upgrades

alternatives.name: Syncthing
alternatives.desc: Syncs the vault directly between computers; iPhones remain the awkward relative.

facts.install: Install a native package or binary on every device, exchange device IDs, and share the vault folder
facts.dataFormat: The original Markdown files and attachments remain as normal files in selected folders on each peer; Syncthing keeps its configuration and index database locally
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no central always-available history or recovery service, devices need overlapping availability to propagate changes, and iPhone/iPad support depends on third-party clients.
facts.setupBlocker: Every device needs a client and pairing, at least one peer must be online to receive changes, and there is no official iOS client

notes: Very clean yes; lets the site distinguish app value from convenience subscription.
prompt:
Build me a sync setup for my Obsidian vault to replace Obsidian Sync. Requirements:

- This is plumbing, not an app: the vault is a folder of Markdown files, sync it with
  git. Syncthing is the zero-history alternative; use git here because I want history.
- A small watcher (Node + chokidar + simple-git, or a plain bash script on a
  systemd/launchd timer, pick the simpler) that debounces 30 seconds after the last
  change, commits with an auto message, and pushes to a private GitHub repo.
- On start and every 5 minutes: pull with rebase. On conflict, never lose data: write
  the incoming version as <name>.conflict-YYYY-MM-DD.md, keep mine in place, and log it.
- .gitignore for .obsidian/workspace* and .trash so device-local state does not ping-
  pong between machines.
- A `vaultsync status` command showing last push/pull time and any outstanding conflict
  files.
- Mobile: point a git client (Working Copy on iOS, MGit on Android) at the same repo.
  Document that in the README, do not build mobile anything.
- The repo stays private; token in .env or the system git credential helper. No accounts
  beyond GitHub, no telemetry, notes stay plain Markdown on disk.
- Out of scope: an encrypted-vault workflow and a version-history UI. git log is the
  history.
- README: second-machine setup steps and the conflict-file convention.
